title: Harwell et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC determined the case judicially out of order and not capable of being put in order because the complaint was not first filed with Nashville Presbytery as required by BCO 43-2; the initial filing was either suggested charges or a call for investigation under BCO 31-2 rather than a complaint against an act or decision under BCO 43-1; and the complainants filed directly with the SJC, with more than sixty days having passed since August 9, 2016. The complaint was dismissed; no merits determination.
first_summary: Complainants sought review of Nashville Presbytery's August 9, 2016 actions. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because it was not first filed with the Presbytery, and the initial filing was not a complaint against an act or decision. More than sixty days had passed, so no further action could be taken. The SJC made no merits ruling.
summary: Complainants sought review of Nashville Presbytery's August 9, 2016 actions but filed directly with the SJC instead of first with Presbytery. The SJC held the complaint judicially out of order and unable to be put in order: the initial filing was not a complaint against an act or decision (BCO 43-1) but suggested charges or an investigation request (BCO 31-2); BCO 43-2 required prior filing with Presbytery, and the sixty-day period had run. The complaint was dismissed without a merits ruling.

sources.supports: Adopted decision, disposition, procedural grounds, and dismissal of the complaint.
